title: 2-Year Treasury Note auction (December new issue) — the year's last front-end sale, sharing Monday 12-28 with the 5-Year and settling on the final business day of 2026
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream into 909 tokens — NOT carried from either proposing sweep's transcription. The row reads verbatim `2-Year NOTE Thursday, December 24, 2026 Monday, December 28, 2026 Thursday, December 31, 2026` (announcement / auction / settlement) with NO trailing `R`, so a new issue; the flag column IS populated three rows above in the same December block (`2-Year FRN R`, `20-Year BOND R`, `5-Year TIPS R T`), so the blank is a signal rather than a missing field. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Read in the same fetch: `5-Year NOTE` on the SAME Monday 12-28, `7-Year NOTE` on Tuesday 12-29, the `13-Week BILL` and `26-Week BILL` also auctioning Monday 12-28 off the same 12-24 announcement, and the schedule's own holiday line `Holiday - Friday, December 25, 2026 - Christmas Day`. STAYS ESTIMATE on the one limit that actually applies at D-110: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this sale is 106 days from its own announcement. The confirming primary is the 2026-12-24 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-09), which read BOTH prior proposals first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md — `proposals/treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28.from-treasury-7y-note-2026-12-29.json` and `proposals/treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28.from-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-24.json`, both filed 2026-09-09. Their date, kind, impact and `symbols: []` are adopted unchanged; their shared headline claim is NOT. TWO CORRECTIONS, both measured this session from Treasury primaries pulled today. (1) THE COMPRESSED-BLOCK RARITY CLAIM IS WRONG AS STATED. The 7Y proposal reads 'A 2Y and 5Y sharing one auction date is common overall (53 of the 152 months since 2014)'. Measured directly off fiscaldata `auctions_query` (nominal notes only — `floating_rate` No AND `inflation_index_security` No; the 2Y monthly slot is `security_term` 2-Year, n=320 since 2000, and the 5Y slot is `original_security_term` 5-Year less the rows that ARE the 2Y slot, n=285): a 2Y and a 5Y have shared an auction date exactly 24 times since 2000, ALL of them since 2017-08, which is 24 of the 152 monthly 2Y slots since 2014 (16%), not 53. More to the point for reading this date: 2026 has ALREADY run this configuration TWICE — 2026-04-27 and 2026-07-27, both $69B, both covering ABOVE their local window (bid-to-cover 2.65 and 2.66 against a $69B-era median of 2.640). This is the third shared session of 2026, not an exotic. (2) THE COMPRESSION PENALTY IS A MONDAY COMPOSITION ARTIFACT, NOT A COMPRESSION EFFECT. The coupon-announcement proposal asks whoever researches this auction to score its block-level finding (z -0.237 vs +0.062, t = -2.67 from 2020-05 onward) rather than re-derive it. Scored: 23 of the 24 shared sessions are MONDAYS, because the 5Y is pulled onto the 2Y's day precisely when the month-end block starts on a Monday. Within Mondays only (2017+), shared vs not-shared 2Y auction-day moves run -0.09bp vs -0.31bp, t = +0.15, permutation p = 0.897 — nothing at all. On demand, inside the $69B era the shared subset is likewise null: bid-to-cover z -0.324 (n=7) vs +0.108 (n=22), p = 0.394; dealer-takedown z +0.283 vs -0.021, p = 0.702. The apparent penalty at the 2Y is the weekday, and the weekday itself is not distinguishable inside the live regime (2023+ far-from-FOMC Mondays -5.22bp, n=9, vs Tuesdays -6.18bp, n=17 — this session reproduces the treasury-2y-note-2026-11-23 sibling's figures exactly). WHAT ACTUALLY MAKES THIS DATE DIFFERENT FROM ITS SIBLINGS, and it cuts against the calendar's -6bp prior twice over. FIRST: December is the WORST month on the 2Y auction-day record (+2.15bp against -0.54bp for every other month, t = +2.59, permutation p = 0.015, n=26) — but that gap decays exactly the way this calendar's Thanksgiving-week discount did, and for the same reason: 2010+ p = 0.227, 2013+ p = 0.358, 2016+ p = 0.512, 2018+ p = 0.727, with the whole 2000+ effect carried by 2003 (+12bp), 2008 (+13bp), 2009 (+9bp), 2007 (+7bp) and 2006 (+6bp). Honest reading: December is NOT a sell-off month once the pre-2010 data is dropped, and it has never been tested inside the current regime beyond n=3 (2023-12-26 -5bp, 2024-12-23 0bp, 2025-12-22 -4bp, mean -3.00bp against the regime's -4.83bp). SECOND, AND THIS ONE SURVIVES EVERY CUT: the Dec-24-to-Dec-31 window is a materially QUIETER tape for the 2-Year. Mean absolute daily 2Y CMT move in that window vs all other sessions runs 2.57bp vs 4.85bp in 2023+ (ratio 0.53, permutation p = 0.073), 2.55 vs 3.80 in 2018+ (ratio 0.67, p = 0.073) and 3.03 vs 3.63 across 2000+ (p = 0.109) — directionally identical in every cut. So the regime's -6bp expectation is about to be applied to a tape that historically moves a third to a half less, which is a SCALING argument, not a sign argument. THIRD: unlike its 11-23 sibling, this auction day is NOT readable. 2026-11-23 carried zero other tracked events; 2026-12-28 carries the 5-Year in the SAME 1:00pm session, the 13-week and 26-week bills at 11:30am, advance-economic-indicators-2026-12-28 at 8:30am, boj-summary-of-opinions-2026-12-28 overnight, two SIFMA closures, and (proposed by this sweep) the Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing survey at 10:30am ET — with fomc-minutes-2026-12-30 two sessions later. Grade this print on its own auction statistics, never on the day's close. SIZE IS NOT PUBLISHED AND MUST NOT BE ASSERTED: press release sb0590, read direct today (HTTP 200, 75,577 bytes), publishes anticipated nominal coupon sizes for `May-26 Jun-26 Jul-26 Aug-26 Sep-26 Oct-26` and STOPS — 2-Year reads 69 in all six rows, and no Treasury document published today names a December figure. $69B is an EXPECTATION from 29 consecutive $69B 2Y prints (2024-04-23 -> 2026-08-25, fiscaldata, zero deviations) plus the release's verbatim flat guidance; the published grid arrives at the 2026-11-04 refunding and the terms at the 12-24 announcement. THE 2020-12-28 TWIN IS WEAKER EVIDENCE THAN THE PROPOSALS SUGGEST: it is a genuine row-for-row calendar twin (same Christmas-Eve announcement, same shared Monday, same 12-31 settlement) and it printed bid-to-cover 2.450 with a 0bp auction-day move — but it sold $58B, 16% less paper than this auction is expected to, into a zero-rate market. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. Ledger: docs/research/events/treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28.md.
